mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3% indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases, it signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the cases when both UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when RSAFS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the cases when INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 indicates a slowdown in the housing market, which may lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the cases when HOUST decreases below 1000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the cases when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases when GDPC1 increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
